title: Kuperberg sieve with rational leading coefficient 3/2 and polynomial quantum space

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, the Kuperberg sieve algorithm and parameter choice described in proof.md (initial pool size O(2^{(3/2) n^{1/2}} n^{2}), O(sqrt(n)) stages, O(n) restarts with cutoff), with n = ceil(log2 N), recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 2/3. In the challenge model this same algorithm has worst-case total work T(N,s) = O(2^{(3/2) n^{1/2}} n^{10}). All constants are absolute. The uniform bit-length envelope B_T(n) = 2^{(3/2) n^{1/2}} n^{10} has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the classical-memory, quantum-memory and sample bounds below.

For the same Kuperberg sieve algorithm and configuration in proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, worst-case peak classical workspace is S_C(N,s) = O(2^{(3/2) n^{1/2}} n^{2}) bits, with n = ceil(log2 N) and an absolute constant. Its envelope B_C(n) = 2^{(3/2) n^{1/2}} n^{2} has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the stated time, quantum-workspace and sample bounds and full-secret success probability at least 2/3.

For the same Kuperberg sieve algorithm and configuration in proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, worst-case peak quantum workspace is S_Q(N,s) = O(n) qubits, with n = ceil(log2 N) and an absolute constant. Its envelope B_Q(n) = n has growth index exactly 0. This holds jointly with the stated time, classical-workspace and sample bounds and full-secret success probability at least 2/3.

For the same Kuperberg sieve algorithm and configuration in proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the total number Q(N,s) of fresh DCP source copies acquired on every execution branch (including all discarded sieve states and failed restarts) is O(2^{(3/2) n^{1/2}} n^{2}). The uniform bit-length envelope B_samples(n) = 2^{(3/2) n^{1/2}} n^{2} has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the stated total-work and workspace bounds and unconditional full-secret success probability at least 2/3.

For the same Kuperberg sieve algorithm and configuration in proof.md, the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n)=0: all Q source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N and s, full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 2/3 jointly with all four resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted; this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: All acquired copies are independent ideal coset states.
